brief: A soldering station for my bench: a holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot, plus two bins for solder and spare tips.

requirements.evidence: No part placed for this. All Hex Cluster parts are 3D-printed plastic and the configurator checks fit only, not heat resistance. A holder holding a switched-on hot iron would soften, melt, or burn. Use a commercial metal soldering stand for the hot iron instead.
requirements.requirement: Holder for the iron while switched on and hot

requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full with solder-reel prop (prop:1), visible from above.
bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 with small-parts prop (prop:2) staging spare tips; no tip prop exists so standoffs stand in.

finish.summary: Built a 2-cell bench caddy with two bins: one for the solder reel and one divided bin for cold spare tips. No holder for a hot, powered iron was built because 3D-printed plastic cannot safely hold a hot iron — use a commercial metal iron stand for that.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

lines.key: pvc-section-double  (cut 18 mm from 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US))
lines.label: pvc-section-double (cut 18 mm from 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US))

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes
